cohort: The study included 4272 women aged 45-59 years with assisted reproductive technology pregnancies, excluding triplet or higher-order multiple gestations, identified from a nationwide registry in Japan.
finding: Women aged 50-54 years had significantly higher risks of adverse pregnancy outcomes including cesarean section, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, placenta previa, placenta accreta, and preterm birth compared to women aged 45-49 years.
mod_finding: Women aged 50-54 years had significantly higher risks of cesarean section, while the instrumental delivery rate was lower, compared to the 45-49 years group.
cross-section timing: Data was collected for pregnancies between January 2013 and December 2022.
